title: Vow of Teeth
logline: An assassin who becomes a leopard by night is sold as a bride to the border warden she is paid to kill. On their wedding night he watches her change, and now one word from his mouth can cage her for life.
central_question: Will Neela kill the husband she was sold to?

heroine_belief.opening: Anyone who truly sees me will put a leash on me.
heroine_belief.changed: Being seen by the right person is the only thing that makes me unleashable.

chapters.title: The Kasavu Bride
chapters.goal: Survive her own wedding unseen and map her target's chamber.
chapters.value_shift: anonymous instrument -> committed to a kill she cannot yet make
beats: Opens mid-rite at sunset on the Kettamala rampart. Neela, in kasavu, counts four exits while Devan closes a plain gold bangle over the ridged resin scar on her left wrist.

Her inner tally sets the society: this is her twelfth contract as ledger number Seventeen, release means her page burned and her birth name returned, and the Monkey Pass closes in about forty days. Janu fusses within earshot that the warden is 32 and too thin, and the bride 27 and too quiet.

At the feast she collects names: Kannan the goat-boy, Chinna in the kitchen, Raiu on the corridor. Devan notices she thanks Raiu by name and asks how she learned it so fast. She answers with a question.

Contract terms surface in Chathu's soft remembered voice: the warden dies in his chamber like a leopard kill, 'not before the marriage writ comes back sealed from Kodiyur, and not after the rains'. She carries the guild's leopard tooth to leave in the wound.
In the chamber Devan answers her questions with exact facts and no comfort. He lays his sword on the floor by her side of the bed, hilt toward her, and says only that he sleeps badly.

She counts three hundred of his breaths, crosses to the west window, opens the teak shutters (the third slat creaks), uncorks the resin and smears throat and wrists. Ends as the burn takes her and her spine begins to bend.
chapters.reader_question_out: Was he really asleep?
chapters.romance_change: From strangers to wary opponents: he notices her habit of naming servants, the first sign to him that she is a person and not a council pawn.

chapters.title: What the Warden Saw
chapters.goal: Learn what the council has put in his bed.
chapters.value_shift: suspicion -> he holds a weapon he refuses to use
beats: Devan lies awake under lowered lids, expecting a knife. Instead he watches the whole turning: the minute of burn, spotted pelt rising over bone, a leopard flowing over the broad ledge into the dark.
He knows the witness rule from border training and lays it out exactly: he is her witness now, and the word cages her only while she is in shape, before dawn, in her hearing. Intent doesn't matter.
Memory of Asha: bear wounds inside walls no bear could climb, an odiyan under contract. Rage pulls him to wait on the ledge and say the word when she returns.

He weighs the case against it: caged, she tells nothing; Muthu would want her dead; the council chose her, so whoever sent her may be the man selling tokens. Under it all is his belief that power is only safe if he never uses it.
He holds the third slat silent and watches the dawn return: shaking, hollow, a woman pulling her sari close on the ledge. He shuts his eyes before she looks his way.
At the cistern chain's dawn clank he asks Janu to leave rice and plantains in the chamber, claiming his own hunger.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will he do with the word?
chapters.romance_change: He sees her at her most exposed and chooses silence; his distrust gains a private, protective edge she cannot see.

chapters.title: Closed Shutters
chapters.goal: Learn the fort's rhythm and find a clean route to the kill.
chapters.value_shift: confident -> blocked by an obstacle she reads as habit
beats: The morning hunger shakes her hands. She assumes the waiting rice is Janu's doing, eats too fast, and hates being seen eating.
Janu tours her through the fort: pepper terraces, the cistern and its hourly chain, the sunken kalari, the padippura. Neela collects guard rotations and names.
On the terrace she asks Devan direct questions. He answers literally. To 'Why did your council choose me?' he says, 'I won't answer that.' She can't make him lie, and it unsettles her.
At dusk she returns to find him closing and barring the west shutters. 'Rain,' he says. The sky is clear. She files it as a fussy habit.
After he sleeps she unbars them to go out, and realises she must bar them again before dawn or he'll know.
Ends at first light as she slides the bar home. The third slat creaks, and she can't tell if he stirred.
chapters.reader_question_out: Is the barred shutter a habit or a trap?
chapters.romance_change: First real sparring talk: she discovers he refuses to lie, which she has never met in a man with power over her.

chapters.title: Kennelled
chapters.goal: Test the household's night defences.
chapters.value_shift: obstacle -> opportunity, then unease
beats: Kannan grumbles that the warden has ordered the hounds kennelled every night since the bride came. The yard is open at night for the first time in years.
Neela argues it both ways in her head. It is either a careless gift to an assassin or bait laid for her.
A patrol rides in with a dead raider's satchel. In the hall Devan breaks a pass-token open and states flatly, in front of Muthu and the men, that the wax is genuine council wax.
She watches him calm a furious sergeant without raising his voice. The competence stirs something she files as threat assessment.
She learns his goal: someone on the queen's council sells the passes. Asked who, he says, 'If I knew, he'd be in a cell.'
That night she crosses the dogless yard as the other one. She stops below his window, aware she wants to know who he is hunting.
chapters.reader_question_out: Who on the council sells the passes, and why did the warden empty the yard?
chapters.romance_change: Attraction begins through his competence, and she learns his goal has nothing to do with her.

chapters.title: The Man Who Doesn't Spar
chapters.goal: Find out who sent her without showing that he knows.
chapters.value_shift: she is an instrument -> she may be a person
beats: Dawn drill alone in the kalari. Muthu, loud and cheerful, begs to spar as he does every week, and Devan refuses as he has for eight years. Muthu's joke covers how much it bothers him.
Devan walks Neela along the pepper terraces and tests her cover. She grades pepper like a Chirayil ward but meets every personal question with a question, and he notices the pattern.
He glimpses the ridged scar under the bangle and says nothing.
She stops to bind Kannan's goat-bitten hand and knows the boy's mother's name. Devan remembers Asha learning every recruit's name, and has to walk away.
At supper Janu starts a leopard story. Devan sees Neela's knuckles whiten on her cup.
He decides to let her try, to watch who she reports to. Quietly, he tells Muthu to pull the night sentry off the west wall below his window, giving no reason.
chapters.reader_question_out: Will his patience protect her or trap her?
chapters.romance_change: He begins to see a will in her: her care for the goat-boy contradicts the instrument he expected.

chapters.title: Green Wax
chapters.goal: Find the household's weak hour.
chapters.value_shift: sure of her ground -> shaken by a word she tells herself is chance
beats: Neela and Janu unpack wedding gifts: a brass lamp from the Chirayil house, and a sandalwood box from the palace sealed in the queen's green wax. Devan cuts the seal and studies it longer than the silver betel set inside.
She asks about the gift. He says plainly that he doesn't trust gifts from the palace.
Janu complains a cat has been at the pepper store and wants the hounds loose again. Devan: 'Leave the cat. It keeps the rats down.' Neela's hand stops on the box lid, then she reasons it away.
Night as the other one, she runs the hill paths. She finds the guild's meeting stone and a fresh jackal scent-mark. Ammu is close.
At dawn she meets the actual pepper-store cat, a scruffy tom, and laughs out loud.
Ends with a jackal's call from the tree line: contact tomorrow.
chapters.reader_question_out: Did he mean the cat?
chapters.romance_change: They share their first distrust, of the palace, which makes them briefly allies against someone else.

chapters.title: There's a Way, Chechi
chapters.goal: Report to the guild without giving away more than she must.
chapters.value_shift: alone -> held by her sister, and given a door she can't open
beats: Market day below the fort. Ammu, disguised as a pepper trader's girl, is humming her fishing song, calls Neela chechi and teases her about the handsome husband.
Ammu passes Chathu's message: the writ is on the road; after it arrives, every day counts; failure means forced resin and Chathu reading Neela's page aloud at dusk.
Ammu has written three letters to Kirri, the released sister, and none has been answered. She jokes that Kirri is busy with her fishing boat. Neela hears the strain under it.
Neela: 'If anyone ever saw me, I'd be finished.' Ammu: 'Not always. There's a way, chechi, but it costs.' She stops herself because she has spotted Muthu at the next stall, and this is guild treason.
Devan arrives to escort Neela home, and she suspects he followed. On the road he quietly clears a soldier's widow's salt debt. Asked why, he says only that the man died on his patrol.
chapters.reader_question_out: What way, and what does it cost?
chapters.romance_change: She witnesses his kindness to someone who can't repay it; the indifference she assumed starts to look like discipline.

chapters.title: The Unlit Lamp
chapters.goal: Narrow the token-seller and learn why the council wanted this marriage.
chapters.value_shift: watching her -> realising the marriage itself may be the weapon
beats: Devan orders the corridor lamp outside his door left unlit after dusk, telling Raiu it saves oil. In truth he wants no light under the door when she slips back at dawn.
He and Muthu compare token wax impressions. Only three council seals could make this mark. Muthu laughs it off as clerks' carelessness.
At noon on the rampart she asks why he never laughs first. He says he waits to learn whether the joke is at someone's expense. She makes one at her own, and he laughs.
He admits nothing about following her to market, and she doesn't ask.
A courier brings the marriage writ back sealed from Kodiyur. Reading it, Devan sees that as his lawful wife, if he dies she holds Kettamala's pass-seal until a new warden is named.
Ends as he looks up and sees Neela's face go still at the sight of the writ.
chapters.reader_question_out: Who wants his widow holding the pass-seal?
chapters.romance_change: First shared laughter; he now suspects she is the weapon, which makes her more valuable to him alive.

chapters.title: The Goat Path
chapters.goal: Study his patrol habits on the road.
chapters.value_shift: contempt for his caution -> respect for his skill
beats: At supper Janu begins a story about a man-eating leopard of the pass. Devan says quietly, 'Not tonight, Janu,' and she stops. Neela decides he simply dislikes stories.
The council expects the bride shown to the pass villages, so Devan takes her down to inspect the lower waystation.
The langurs fall silent: strangers on the road. A rockfall blocks the cart road.
Neela leads them down a goat path she knows without a map, and she cannot say how she knows it. He asks, and she answers with a question.
At the waystation he reads the raider tracks and she reads the boot-wear. Neither could do the other's half.
Riding home at dusk without resin, she is human beside him under the first heavy clouds, and lets herself enjoy it for one mile.
chapters.reader_question_out: How does she know the pass?
chapters.romance_change: A competence duet: each reads what the other can't, and respect enters the enmity.

chapters.title: The Broken Beak
chapters.goal: Plan the kill now that the writ is sealed.
chapters.value_shift: a window open -> a plan he has quietly made impossible
beats: Neela walks the west stair to map an approach. Her hand closes on the parrot newel's broken beak and her stomach drops. She counts the steps and cannot stop counting.
Janu mentions that the warden has barred his shutters every dusk since the wedding, never once before, and the whole fort knows it.
Neela sees the problem: a leopard kill inside a barred room points straight at the bride. She lists whether he did it on purpose or by chance.
Night: as the other one she comes through the shutters she unbarred and stands over him. His hand lies open on the blanket, old scars on the knuckles. The kindi on her side has been filled.
She cannot make the kill look like a beast, and tells herself that is the only reason. She leaves.
Ends at dawn with a new plan: the kalari, before first light, human hands, marma.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can she kill him with her hands?
chapters.romance_change: She stands over him with the power to kill and finds herself studying him instead; her tactical reason for holding back is wearing thin.

chapters.title: Dawn Drill
chapters.goal: Kill him in the kalari with a marma strike.
chapters.value_shift: resolved killer -> a woman who failed on purpose
beats: Before dawn she takes the path to the kalari through lantana. The smell of crushed leaves makes her gag, a hatred she has never understood.
She watches him drill, faster and deadlier than anyone she has seen, striking only air.
She steps down into the pit and asks for a form. He refuses to spar. She offers to correct his stance instead, and he allows it.
Her fingers rest at the base of his skull, on the killing point, clean. She counts three breaths. She lifts her hand and tells him his guard drops on the left.
He says, 'You'd have had me.' She says, 'Yes.' Neither explains.
She climbs out shaking and lies to herself in the chamber about why.
chapters.reader_question_out: Why did she pull it, and why did he let her stand there?
chapters.romance_change: She declines a clean chance to kill him and he knows it; it is the first choice each recognises in the other.

chapters.title: Parrots
chapters.goal: Decide what a woman who pulled her strike is worth to him.
chapters.value_shift: a tool to watch -> a will to bargain with
beats: Devan revises his view: she had him and didn't kill him, and a woman with a will can be bargained with.
Janu asks him at last to clear Asha's chest. He finds her notes, each signed with a drawn parrot, and the first forged token Asha found. Its wax matches the new tokens.

Neela finds him there. He tells her about Asha: his second at the fort, fearless with soldiers, afraid of the dark, killed six years ago under contract. To 'How?' he says, 'I won't answer that.' In his head, unsaid, are the west stair and the bear wounds.
Neela reads one of Asha's notes, laughs at the right line, and asks what Asha would want now. He answers truly and feels less alone with her.
That evening he sees Muthu hand a plain-sealed letter to the palace rider. Muthu laughs and says it's for his mother, and Devan believes him.
Ends with Asha's line in his hand, 'the truth protects whoever finds it'. He decides to offer the bargain.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will he ask for, and what will he give?
chapters.romance_change: First real disclosure: he gives her Asha and her attention moves him, while the reader sees the dread he can't.

chapters.title: The Cat on the Sill
chapters.goal: Devan: survive a fever without speaking the word. Neela: keep him alive though his death would suit her.
chapters.value_shift: hidden guard -> guard held by a bitten tongue
beats: Devan rides in with a raider arrow-graze gone bad. By evening he has a fever, and the fort physician bleeds him and despairs.
Neela takes over. She knows the marma healing points and how to clean a wound, and she tells Janu what to boil. Her guild report is due tonight.
Through fever Devan watches her take resin at dusk and turn again. The leopard settles on the sill to keep watch.

Janu sees eyes on the ledge and cries out about an animal. Devan feels the word on his tongue, starts it, and bites down until he tastes blood: 'It's the cat. Leave the cat. Draw the curtain.' Janu saw only eyes, not a turning, and is no witness.
Neela's scene, in shape: she hears him rave about a cat and thinks nothing of it. The reader knows she just lived through a caging by a hair.
At dawn she turns back on the ledge while he sleeps. The fever breaks. She sits hollow on the floor by the bed and does not leave.
chapters.reader_question_out: How long can he keep the word behind his teeth?
chapters.romance_change: She chooses to keep him alive when his death by fever would end her problem; he guards her with his own blood.

chapters.title: Varanad Coin
chapters.goal: Find out who is hunting the patrol.
chapters.value_shift: neutral to his survival -> his protector, at the cost of her way out
beats: Devan insists on riding the dawn patrol through the lower narrows while still weak. Muthu argues, and Neela hears the route.
At dusk, as the other one, she scents two raider scouts camped above the narrows with bows and a signal mirror, waiting for dawn.
Her choice: if he dies in an ambush she is free of the job without blame. She kills both scouts, and refuses the animal's hunger after.
Their satchel holds Varanad-minted silver and a forged token. She drags it onto the patrol path where it will be found.
She turns back at dawn among the rocks, freezing, and walks home. From the terrace she watches his patrol find the mauled scouts, the coin and the token. He looks up at the hills for a long time.
At supper he says the pepper-store cat has been busy. She can't tell if he is joking.
chapters.reader_question_out: Why would raiders carry Varanad coin, and does he know who saved him?
chapters.romance_change: Her first chosen act of protection costs her the clean way out; he thanks her sideways.

chapters.title: First Storm
chapters.goal: Get home before first light.
chapters.value_shift: hidden -> seen, and offered a leash
beats: The monsoon's first storm breaks while she tracks couriers far down the ridge as the other one. The rain wipes out scent, and she misjudges the hour.
She reaches the ledge as dawn takes her, half-turned, fur sloughing to skin. Devan is sitting on the bed, awake, watching the whole return.
He tells her he saw her on the wedding night. He has been her witness for twenty days.
She counts her witnesses: Chathu, Ammu, him. She reaches under the mattress for the knife, and he does not move.

He offers the bargain once: his silence for the name of whoever bought his death. She refuses. She doesn't know the name, and if she did she wouldn't buy her life from a man who can take it with one word.
He says, 'Then we both know where we stand,' and goes to drill. She sits shaking on the sill with the rain blowing in.
chapters.reader_question_out: Now that he holds the word openly, will he use it?
chapters.romance_change: The secret breaks: he is her witness, and his offer turns her husband into one more master.

chapters.title: Terms Withdrawn
chapters.goal: Devan: decide what kind of man made that offer. Neela: find the trap in his gift.
chapters.value_shift: master and captive -> a gift she cannot trust
beats: Devan stands in the kalari and cannot drill. He hears his offer in a guild master's voice: he made himself her master, the thing he swore never to be.
At dusk he says it aloud: the bargain was the guild's leash in his mouth. He withdraws it with no terms. His silence is hers, freely.
Neela's scene: she asks why. 'Because I don't want to own anyone.'

She rereads the first half: the shutters barred at dusk so no servant saw her turn, the hounds kennelled so they wouldn't bay at a leopard, 'the cat', the unlit lamp, Janu's stories stopped, rice after every hungry morning.
Her life allows one conclusion: a hunter's patience, saving the word for when she is most useful caged.
Still, as an experiment, she sleeps that night without resin, human, her back to him, the knife untouched.
chapters.reader_question_out: Is his gift mercy or patience?
chapters.romance_change: First real choice: he gives up power over her with no terms, and her refusal to trust it is rational and costs them both.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Letter
chapters.goal: Learn to live beside a witness who claims no rights.
chapters.value_shift: cover identities -> truthful adversaries
beats: New terms of living: in the dark they talk plainly. She asks, and he answers or says he won't.

Councillor Ittan's letter arrives, genial and wordy, every line 'my friend'. He will come himself to seal the pass for the monsoon, and asks after the warden's bride, 'such a comfort, should anything befall the fort'.
Devan reads it aloud. Neela marks the phrase. Devan lists his suspects: three council seals, and Muthu's palace rider.
She asks why he hasn't asked for the name again. 'I said no terms.'
A jackal's call: report tomorrow. About seventeen days remain.
She lies awake wanting to give him something she doesn't have.
chapters.reader_question_out: Is the genial Keeper a friend, or the hand on the knife?
chapters.romance_change: Honest talk replaces cover, and the silence between them becomes something both choose.

chapters.title: Kirri's Anklet
chapters.goal: Keep Ammu satisfied without exposing him.
chapters.value_shift: loyal to her sister -> lying to her for him
beats: At the meeting stone by day, Ammu is sharper than before. Chathu is impatient.
Ammu remembers that Kirri swore she'd send her silver anklet as a sign once she had her boat. It never came, and Ammu's fear shows through her chatter.
Neela does not tell Ammu that Devan is her witness: her first lie to her sister, told to protect him. Ammu pushes and gets questions back.
Ammu states her creed that they're safe as long as nobody but them has seen. Neela can't argue, because it has kept them alive.
Evening: Janu teaches the fort's pebble game, seven wells. Neela cheats, Devan catches her and is delighted, and cheats back. The hall laughs and Muthu roars.
Ends with Neela alone, booking the lie and the laugh as the same debt.
chapters.reader_question_out: Where is Kirri?
chapters.romance_change: Lightness between them for the first time, bought with a lie to her sister; it is the first price she pays for him.

chapters.title: Resin on the Rampart
chapters.goal: Hunt for Ammu's report.
chapters.value_shift: wanting -> kissed, and caught
beats: Ammu demands a night report. At sunset on the east rampart, where she means to go over the wall, Neela smears resin on throat and wrists. She has about a minute.
Devan steps out of the cistern housing. They talk about Asha's fear of the dark and about Neela's counting. He says he'd like to know what she counts.
She kisses him, knowing the clock. The turning will start in front of him if she stays, Ammu watches from the tree line, and one careless word from him could cage her.
At the first burn she breaks away mid-kiss and runs for the stair. He doesn't follow, and she notices.
She turns in the stair's shadow. From the wall as the leopard she sees a jackal's eyes at the tree line. Ammu saw.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will Ammu do with what she saw?
chapters.romance_change: Desire is declared in action; the rule interrupts it, and the kiss becomes evidence in Ammu's hands.

chapters.title: The Name Given Back
chapters.goal: Keep Ammu from reporting, and make the nights safe.
chapters.value_shift: the word as her burden -> the word as his responsibility
beats: Ammu confronts her: 'You kissed the mark.' It is fear for Neela, not reproach. Ammu will report nothing for one more week.
Ammu hums, then sings a verse of an old tappers' song about 'the name given back at the closing of day'. Neela asks what it means. Ammu says it's only a song and changes the subject.
Ammu warns that Chathu sends Vellan if there's no kill by the new moon.

That night in the dark Neela asks Devan to promise never to say it. He won't promise what depends on sleep or fever. Instead he shows her the old watchman's trick, a smooth river pebble in the cheek, and keeps one there every resin night from now on.
She laughs, then stops. No one has ever made the word their problem instead of hers.
chapters.reader_question_out: What name, given back to whom?
chapters.romance_change: Responsive care: he takes on the danger of his own mouth in a way she can see, and she lets him.

chapters.title: The Captain at Twenty-Four
chapters.goal: Answer her honestly when she finally asks.
chapters.value_shift: guarded -> wanting her at his back
beats: Rain-locked day. They trade a question for a question, each costing more.
She asks why he won't spar. At 24 a raider captain surrendered, knelt and spat at him. Devan struck one marma point in anger and killed him, and has struck no living person since.
She doesn't absolve him. She names exactly what he did and that he stopped, and he feels understood rather than forgiven.
Her disclosure: a number, not a name. Seventeen. She learns every servant's name because no one ever learned hers.
Night: asleep, she counts steps under her breath and whimpers at something broken. Devan holds still and thinks it is the guild in her dreams.
He realises he wants her at his back.
chapters.reader_question_out: What stair does she count in her sleep?
chapters.romance_change: Mutual disclosure at cost: she sees his restraint as fear, and he sees her naming habit as grief.

chapters.title: A Night Without Resin
chapters.goal: Spend one night as a woman beside him, by choice.
chapters.value_shift: hidden body -> seen body, and a name in her hand
beats: She chooses no resin tonight. The night counts toward the ache, and Ammu's signal at the stone will be missed.
At dusk she opens the shutters herself and stays human. In lamplight she shows him the scars at her throat and wrists. He asks before he touches, and she sets each term.
Explicit scene, consensual and specific to them: his restraint meets her direction. She asks him to stay till morning, and he does.
She wakes once in the dark and adds the night to her count without regret.
Morning at the stone: Ammu covered the missed signal by going out as the jackal herself, so the guild's watcher logged both, a reckless dare.
Ammu hands over a slip stolen from Chathu's accounts: 'Balance due from the Keeper on the widow's seal.' Neela understands: the Keeper of the Passes, Ittan.
chapters.reader_question_out: Will she tell him?
chapters.romance_change: First intimacy turns silence given into presence chosen: she is seen as a human woman on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Name
chapters.goal: Keep his word not to ask.
chapters.value_shift: suspicion -> alliance
beats: Dawn kalari. Neela comes down the steps and gives him the name unasked, with the slip: Ittan.
He connects it all: the council wax, the letter, the writ condition, the widow holding the seal, Ittan taking it from her.
He wants to ride for Kodiyur. She points out that the pass closes in eight days, and Ittan is coming to them.
Values collision: he wants her to testify before the queen. She won't. A confessed odiyan before the crown is a rogue to be hunted, and Ammu's page sits in the same ledger.
He accepts her limit. They plan to use border law: every cart through the padippura on sealing day is searched, including the Keeper's.
She asks him to spar. 'Not yet,' he says, but not never.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can they trap a councillor before the guild's deadline falls?
chapters.romance_change: She gives freely what he once tried to buy; trust becomes rational for him, and they become allies with a shared plan.

chapters.title: The Carved Bird
chapters.goal: Devan: find who else reports on him. Neela: buy time from the guild.
chapters.value_shift: a plan in hand -> the enemy already inside
beats: Devan sees Muthu hand another letter to the palace rider. When asked, Muthu goes very quiet. Devan suspects he is Ittan's man and decides to keep him close rather than accuse.
Neela goes to the stone and finds Vellan, not Ammu. He is blunt and sparing: 'New moon, Seventeen. Or I do it and you go home in a collar.'
He whittles a small bird as they talk and says the blade isn't guilty, only the hand. She asks after Kirri, and he doesn't answer.
She warns Devan about Vellan but keeps his night-shape to herself, a guild-sister's line she won't cross. Devan says he'll double the watch. She says watches don't stop him.
Ends with a carved wooden bird on her pillow inside the barred chamber. Vellan has already been in.
chapters.reader_question_out: When will Vellan strike, and where?
chapters.romance_change: She warns him openly about her own guild, choosing his life over guild silence, and he trusts her warning over his own read of Muthu.

chapters.title: Claw Marks
chapters.goal: Get through the new moon alive.
chapters.value_shift: guarded -> poisoned, and unable to stop her
beats: New moon dusk. Devan climbs the west stair at the hour chain. Vellan, human, steps from behind the parrot newel and cuts him across the ribs with a blade smeared dark.
Devan blocks and gives ground but won't strike. Raiu runs up the stair. Vellan, resin already on, turns on the steps into a sloth bear and mauls Raiu.
Bleeding, Devan sees the claw marks on Raiu's chest: a bear, inside the walls, on this stair. The thought of Asha flares, and the poison scatters it.
Neela arrives human, having skipped resin to guard him. The bear sees her and goes over the wall.
Raiu dies under her hands as she says his name. The physician names the poison: blackbark gall. Neela says the only antidote is at the Resin House and gives it three days.
She saddles in the stable. Devan grips her wrist: 'If you go there, they'll cage you.' His grip fails mid-word as the poison takes him.
chapters.reader_question_out: Will she walk back into the guild for him, and can she come out?
chapters.romance_change: He finally sees what she will risk for him and can't stop her; she chooses to walk back into her own cage.

chapters.title: The Kennels
chapters.goal: Steal the antidote and ride back.
chapters.value_shift: a sister of the guild -> its prisoner, seeing the truth
beats: She leaves Muthu orders: keep Devan cool, and follow with him to the Resin House if she isn't back by the second dusk. Then a day's hard ride through rain into the Blackbark Wood.
The bitter scorched-tamarind smell of resin. She takes a vial of antidote from the tapping-shed cupboard, then meets a sloth bear in the yard and the hunters behind it.
She is dragged to the kennels: rows of cages, animals with dimming eyes. One is a civet wearing a silver anklet. Kirri. Release is a lie.
At dawn Chathu comes, soft and patient, the ledger under his arm, speaking of debts and balances: 'The ledger is mercy.' Then: 'And the ledger isn't the only book, child.'
He binds her. At dusk he will force resin on her and read her page, and Vellan will finish the warden.
Ammu, recalled to the yard, meets Neela's eyes across the bars.
chapters.reader_question_out: Will Ammu choose the guild or her sister?

chapters.title: Leopard
chapters.goal: Live free, and keep him alive.
chapters.value_shift: about to be caged -> uncageable, and bereaved
beats: Before sunset Chathu's hunters force the resin onto her throat and wrists. The scars tear and bleed, and she will turn at dusk whatever she does.

Ammu unlocks the kennel, cuts her bonds, gives back the antidote vial and tells her the self-naming loophole: once in a life, to one person who is looking, during the dusk turning; it voids every other witness, the pair share wounds, and she goes rogue. 'I didn't tell you because it costs, chechi, and because hiding kept us alive.'
Devan rides in, grey with poison, held in the saddle by Muthu. Muthu stays to fight at the gatehouse and never sees the yard. Neela pours the antidote into Devan's mouth.
Sunset. Chathu steps out with her page. Neela turns to face Devan, and as the burn takes her she says in her human voice, to him, 'Leopard.'
Chathu reads the page aloud and nothing happens. The witness entry blackens and burns in his hands.
Vellan, as the bear, charges the downed Devan and the leopard. Devan strikes his first blow at a living creature in eight years, a marma strike to the bear's shoulder that breaks the charge.
Ammu turns jackal and draws Vellan and the hunters into the trees. Neela, voiceless in shape, hears the spear and the jackal's last cry.
She cannot turn back before dawn. She lies across Devan in the mud and does not leave.
chapters.reader_question_out: What is left of them at first light?
chapters.romance_change: She gives him the word that could have caged her and makes him the only witness who matters; he uses his power openly, and violently, to protect her.

chapters.title: Wound-Share
chapters.goal: Neela: bury her sister. Devan: face the man who bought his death.
chapters.value_shift: grief -> resolve
beats: At first light she turns back across Devan. The gash on his ribs opens as a red welt along her own side, and she understands she will feel him for life.
Ammu's body lies in the trees. Neela says her name, closes her eyes, and keeps her resin pouch. Muthu digs the grave.
Chathu has fled into the Blackbark Wood with the ledger and Vellan. Caging can't be undone, so Neela cannot free Kirri, and she promises to come back for all of them in the kennels.
The ride home. She is rogue now, her guild entry burned.
Devan's scene: day 39. Ittan's carts climb to the padippura for the sealing. Ittan sees Devan alive and doesn't miss a step: 'My friend!'
Devan probes. Ittan, genial: 'I am only a hand, my friend. Hands go where they're sent.'
chapters.reader_question_out: Whose hand is he?
chapters.romance_change: Bound in body: the wound-share makes his pain hers, and grief makes them each other's only household.

chapters.title: The Sealing
chapters.goal: Arrest Ittan with proof before the pass closes.
chapters.value_shift: power withheld -> power used openly
beats: Sealing day, in rain. Devan orders the Keeper's carts searched under border law, his first open use of authority against the council.
Muthu hesitates, then obeys. Neela stands beside Devan in public as his wife, by her own choice.
In a false-bottomed chest: blank pass-tokens in council wax and Ittan's private tally. The wax impression matches the token from Asha's chest.
Neela produces Chathu's slip, the Keeper's balance on the widow's seal. Devan reads the writ condition aloud: the widow holds the seal.
Ittan's geniality cracks. Devan arrests him under the padippura roof. Ittan: 'You've no idea whose hand I am.'
Devan seals the pass with the warden's seal. The monsoon arrives in full, and Kettamala is cut off for four months.
chapters.reader_question_out: Who sent Ittan?
chapters.romance_change: He uses power openly with her at his side, and she stands seen before the whole fort as his wife rather than his cover.

chapters.title: The Tooth
chapters.goal: Tell him everything.
chapters.value_shift: allies -> lovers who have chosen with full knowledge
beats: At dusk she opens the west shutters herself and leaves them open. She no longer needs to hide a turning from the only witness who counts.
She gives him the leopard tooth she was meant to leave in his wound, and tells him the whole contract.
He answers the question he refused in chapter 3: he barred the shutters on the second dusk so no one but him would see her, because he had already decided never to use what he'd seen.
He tells her when he decided to trust her: her fingers at the base of his skull, and three counted breaths.
Recognition: being seen by him is the only thing that has made her unleashable. He used his power yesterday, openly, and is still himself.
Both say they love each other in plain words; he never lies, so she believes him. She asks him to marry her again, in daylight, with her choice in it this time.
chapters.reader_question_out: What does a vow mean when nothing is hidden?
chapters.romance_change: Recognition and declaration: each names the change in themselves and chooses the other with full knowledge.

chapters.title: Daylight Vows
chapters.goal: Marry him in truth.
chapters.value_shift: a bargain -> a marriage
beats: Noon in the courtyard, before Janu, Muthu, Kannan, Chinna and the garrison, under rain-dark sky. Neela speaks her own vow, naming the dead, Raiu and Ammu, and every living soul in the house she has learned.
Janu weeps, complains about the rain, and overfeeds everyone. Grief and laughter sit side by side.
At dusk she uses Ammu's resin and turns at the open window in front of him on purpose. He sets his pebble on the sill. He doesn't need it now that a caging needs both voices, but he keeps it.
The leopard sleeps the night along his side.
At first light she turns back in his arms, the first time she has let anyone see the return.
Explicit scene in the dawn, which she leads. He kisses the scars, she touches the healing ribs whose twin welt she carries, and they talk about the future aloud.
chapters.reader_question_out: How long can a fort cut off by rain keep them safe?
chapters.romance_change: Betrothal: married in truth; she lets him witness her return by choice, and what was a kept secret becomes a shared life.

chapters.title: The Queen's Seal
chapters.goal: Close the case against Ittan.
chapters.value_shift: safe for the season -> facing the crown itself
beats: In the rain-dark records room Devan goes through Ittan's effects: token-sale ledgers, and a letter to his invalid wife's physicians that shows real devotion.
Wrapped in oilcloth is the guild's contract chit for the warden of Kettamala, bearing Chathu's mark, and the payment writ that bought it.
The writ's seal is green wax, the queen's own. He sets it beside the seal from the palace wedding gift. They are the same.
He takes it straight to Neela without hiding it, which is the whole of his change.
Neela asks the next question: if the crown paid the guild, what else does the queen own?

Teaser: four months before the pass opens, Kirri in the kennels, Chathu holding the ledger. She says she is going to take it, and he says he will come. On the hall table lies Muthu's latest letter, waiting for the roads to open.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can they steal the ledger without becoming its new masters?
chapters.romance_change: Partners against the crown: he shares the most dangerous fact in the realm with her at once, and she plans the next fight as his equal.
